provenanceIsTheHeadlineHere.what: Instagram itself labels this account **AI content**. The label appears under the handle on the captured slides, applied by the platform rather than claimed by us.
provenanceIsTheHeadlineHere.theTension: The caption is written in the first person and says the notes come from highlights the author WATCHED. An AI-content label and a first-hand viewing claim cannot both be taken at face value. This file does not attempt to adjudicate which is true — it records that the two are in tension, because a reader coming to this capture later needs that before they weigh anything in it.
provenanceIsTheHeadlineHere.whyItChangesTheWeightAndNotTheFacts: It does NOT make the content wrong; the checks below found it accurate wherever it was checkable. What it changes is what the source IS. Tom Hadley publishes a stated method (bookmaker odds plus last season's home/away record) under a named identity and can be held to it. An account the platform marks as AI-generated offers assertions with no method behind them and no one accountable for them, and its agreement with our register is therefore weak evidence about the world — it may simply be reproducing the same public inputs we read.
provenanceIsTheHeadlineHere.consequenceForGrading: Graded SEPARATELY from the human-authored captures. Pooling its calls with Hadley's or the tipsters' would let a generated opinion count as a second witness, which is exactly the double-counting the EFL round-1 file already warns about for correlated picks.

aBugInOurOwnChecker.what: The first price pass reported Vuskovic at '£5m vs ours £21.5m' and Van Hecke at '£5m vs ours £22.5m'. Both were TRANSFER FEES read out of the signing lines, not FPL prices.
aBugInOurOwnChecker.why: A fee and a game price are both a number in pounds beside a player's name, and nothing but surrounding context separates them. A regex that scans for the nearest pound figure will find whichever comes first.
aBugInOurOwnChecker.fixed: The pattern now requires the marker the register puts on a settled price. Two manufactured conflicts avoided — the same failure shape as the surname collisions in the set-piece diff and the departure-in-prose miscount in the S7S capture.
aBugInOurOwnChecker.andItMattersHere: Had those two been recorded, this file would open by accusing an AI-labelled source of inventing prices, on evidence that was entirely our own parsing error. The provenance note above would have made that accusation look plausible, which is precisely why it needed checking rather than assuming.

convergesWithOurOwnReadOnPalmer.theirClaim: 'Morgan Rogers is the attacker I would rather back over Palmer because the value feels much stronger' and 'Palmer (£9.5m) is still a strong pick, but right now he is not where I want to spend.'
convergesWithOurOwnReadOnPalmer.ourIndependentRead: From Tom Hadley's consistency table, captured earlier today: Palmer at £9.5m had a 38% 4+ points hit rate last season, the weakest per pound of the premium group — against Bruno Fernandes 71%, Gabriel 77% and Joao Pedro's 89% bonus-from-one-return.
convergesWithOurOwnReadOnPalmer.whatThatIsWorth: Two sources reaching the same conclusion by different routes — one from a stated last-season consistency table, one from watching (or claiming to watch) pre-season. It is NOT two independent confirmations in the strong sense: an AI-authored account may well be reading the same public tables. Recorded as convergence, not corroboration.
convergesWithOurOwnReadOnPalmer.andItIsGradeable: Palmer's actual GW1-6 return against Rogers' settles it.

theIgorThiagoPriceConflict.ourRegister: 'Igor Thiago (FWD, ~£7.0-7.5m est.)' — an ESTIMATE, explicitly marked est., never settled against a published price
theIgorThiagoPriceConflict.status: UNRESOLVED, and deliberately not settled here.
theIgorThiagoPriceConflict.whyNotSettled: Every previous price row settled this season went the same way: seven of eight resolved rows had the outside figure right and ours wrong, so the base rate says an outside number beats our estimate. But this source is the one carrying an AI-content label, and 'our estimates usually lose' is not a reason to accept a figure from a source with no stated method and nobody accountable for it. A price is exactly the kind of hard, checkable number a generated account could get wrong without any tell.
theIgorThiagoPriceConflict.howToSettleIt: The FPL bootstrap prices every player. Unreachable from this sandbox, trivially reachable from CI — and the app itself shows the live price.
theIgorThiagoPriceConflict.whyItMattersBeyondTheRegister: It travels. Advice given in this session said that swapping Igor Thiago for Calvert-Lewin at £6.0m 'costs you the same £6.0m'. That was asserted without a source. Our own register had Thiago at ~£7.0-7.5m est. and this slide says £8.0m, so on either figure the swap FREES money rather than being neutral — between £1.0m and £2.0m, which is the difference between a thin defence and a workable one in a squad built around six premiums.
theIgorThiagoPriceConflict.theProcessPoint: The number was stated confidently, was not in the register at the price claimed, and nothing checked it because nothing was looking at prices quoted in conversation. Same shape as the rest of the fortnight.
